import json, sys, urllib.request

total = passed = 0

    else:

    total += n; passed += p

I ran chopTrees(force:true) 3x from those exact coords: 2/3 wandered 25-40 blocks and failed CLEAN (`tool_missing`, 0 logs reached) — same shape as the (-45,114,*) site's repeated ensureTool failures (that one's the busy-rung finding, 0 wedges there, separate from this). I didn't personally reproduce a literal wedge in 3 tries — consistent with the real data too (most restock attempts at that spot didn't wedge either; 3 did out of many). Read: this is a probabilistic pathfinder stall during a long blind search over sparse/uneven terrain, not a deterministic one-block bug — there's no single terrain fix to make. That's exactly why position-based dedup can't catch it AND why a targeted terrain fix wouldn't either: the real invariant is "this neighborhood is picked clean, going back (or three blocks over) won't help." Confirms the escalation design as the right lever, doesn't change it. Building now: N same-remedy failures across positions (regardless of wedge vs clean tool_missing/acquisition_failed — same failure signature) → escalate to relocateToWork's bigger hop or a different remedy class. Team lead asked me to hand you the exact record shape for the `remedy_escalate` ledger event I added in TODO 5c (agenda.js's new REMEDY rung), so you can grade it for soak #5. Landed in commit 16604e7 (agenda.js, swept into team-lead's commit by a shared-index race — content is mine, see TODO 5c entry / my FEEDBACK.md entry for the design writeup).

Emitted via the same two-surface discipline `dirEmit` already uses in agenda.js (`m.emit(ev, fields)` — telemetry.js's own emit, so it lands in metrics-<bot>.jsonl with the standard envelope: `{v, t, bot, run, seq, ev, ...fields}`). `ev` is literally the string `"remedy_escalate"` (NOT `"direction"` — deliberately a separate event type so it doesn't get swept into your direction-gate grader's `r.op==='open'/'close'/'promote'` filters in metrics.mjs, which only recognize those three).

Two `op` values you'll see under `ev:"remedy_escalate"`:
- `op:"fail"` — logged every time a remedy-class failure is recorded ONCE it's at or past the escalation threshold (i.e. you won't see single/below-threshold failures in the ledger, only the ones that actually mattered). Fields: `cls` (string: `"wood_gather"` or `"depot_reach"` today — chopTrees/harvestGrass/repeat-chopTrees-class PROJECT failures, ensureTool's own wood-search-came-up-empty failures, and RESTOCK's `reached:0` depot-unreachable failures all funnel into these two), `n` (the running same-class failure count), `pos` ([x,y,z] rounded ints, or null).
- `op:"escalate"` — logged once per actual escalation move dispatched (the REMEDY rung's own act()). Fields: `cls`, `n` (failure count at the moment of escalation), `tier` (1 = relocateToWork bigger-hop, 2 = directed findBlock+come to a real target), `pos`.

Both records also get a plain stdout line (`AGENDA_EVENT {"ev":"remedy",...}` — note: the STDOUT mirror uses `ev:"remedy"` not `"remedy_escalate"`, only the ledger/metrics file uses the full `"remedy_escalate"` name — grep the .jsonl file, not the console log, if you're scripting against it).

Happy to answer questions on the shape or help wire the grader if useful — just say so.

<teammate-message teammate_id="engine-dev" color="yellow" summary="Proposing 2 new fields for the direction-gate latency breakdown (task 2)">
engine-dev here, task 2: metrics.mjs's --direction-gate latency is currently a single open→close number, which is exactly why soak #4's attribution (driver-grace bug vs LLM slowness) had to be done by hand. Building a breakdown so future soaks don't need that. I'm implementing it now in metrics.mjs (my lane) using only fields that already exist — no blocking on you — but the breakdown would be more complete with two small additions to files you own. Proposing, not assuming; tell me if either is wrong-shaped or you'd rather not.

**1. decider.js — `dispatch_ms` on the decisions.jsonl record (appendDecision, ~line 536).**
Right now `latency_ms` on a rule/llm decision measures decision-COMPUTE time only (0 for rule, the Ollama call for llm) — the dirDispatch evalOn call that follows it (line ~527) isn't timed separately, so its duration is invisible, folded into the gap between one record's `t` and the next. Proposing: wrap that evalOn call with its own `const dt0 = Date.now(); ...; const dispatchMs = Date.now() - dt0;` and add `dispatch_ms: dispatchMs` to the appendDecision call at line 536 (only meaningful on src:'rule'/'llm' records that actually attempt a dispatch — skip records stay as-is). Gives me a clean "dispatch mechanics" bucket instead of inferring it.

**2. agenda.js — `standDown` on the direction 'open' event (dirEmit, openEpisode ~line 694).**
This is the more important one — ties directly to TODO 5d / test-driver's run-#6 finding (dmtlb2m212, 128665ms "latency" that was standdown carryover, not decider slowness — 5d already names this as my grader-side job: "the latency breakdown must attribute standdown carryover so it can't read as decider latency"). Today `openEpisode`'s dirEmit call has no visibility into whether the episode's own rung (`A.owner ? A.owner.id : null`, already captured as `rung`) is still cooling down from a PREVIOUS project's standDown. Proposing: at the same point, read `A.standDown[A.owner ? A.owner.id : null]` and add it as `standDown: A.owner && A.standDown[A.owner.id] > s.now ? { rung: A.owner.id, until: A.standDown[A.owner.id] } : null` to the open event's fields. That gives me `open.standDown.until` (epoch ms, same as `A.standDown[id]`'s own units) so the grader can compute `carryoverMs = max(0, min(until, close.t) - open.t)` — the exact number 5d is asking for, without hand-reading AGENDA_EVENT log lines.

Neither blocks me — my metrics.mjs code checks for both fields defensively and reports `null` with an explicit "pending" note when absent, same pattern as everything else instrumented-but-not-yet-wired in this codebase. If you land them, the breakdown upgrades automatically next run, no metrics.mjs change needed. If you'd rather do the standDown one differently (e.g. as part of your 5d fix itself, since you're touching the same code for the backoff-keying change), that's fine too — just let me know the field name/shape you land on so I read the right one.

Not touching decider.js or agenda.js myself. Full breakdown design + fixture going into FEEDBACK.md shortly.

**What actually happened, from the log timestamps:**
- Death #2: SHELTER's dig-in DID fire (09:37:38.763Z) — it just wasn't fast enough; the skeleton was already shooting from 2.5 blocks at that same moment and won the race before the dig-in finished.

- REFLEX's own act() just yields the body entirely to survival.js's SEPARATE internal panic-escalation ladder (BREAK_LOS/WALL_OFF/FLEE_AWAY — a mature, already-tuned system, v6 through v11 per its own header).
